prompt:
You are a decision-support tool for a radiologist. Review this patient's frontal chest X-ray and report on six findings. A radiologist checks your output; give your best assessment. Findings and their definitions: - Lung Opacity: airspace opacity, consolidation, infiltrate or airspace disease in the lung. A discrete nodule or mass is not Lung Opacity (it is Lung Lesion). - Cardiomegaly: an enlarged heart. A borderline or upper-normal heart size counts as absent. - Atelectasis: collapse or incomplete expansion of lung tissue, including subsegmental or plate-like atelectasis. - Lung Lesion: a nodule, mass or cavity in the lung. A calcified granuloma does not count. - Pleural Effusion: fluid in the pleural space. - Fracture: a fracture of the ribs, clavicles, spine or any other visible bone. Healed or old fractures count. How to work: 1. Read the patient's image systematically first. 2. Then look at the 10 most similar cases from a reference database, listed below with their reports. They are other patients whose images look similar to this one. Use them as supporting evidence to confirm or question what you see in the patient's image, not as the answer: a finding in a similar case does not mean that this patient has it. 3. Take the clinical indication into account. 4. For each of the six findings, give its status (present, absent or uncertain), the probability (0 to 1) that it is present in this patient, the IDs of the similar cases that support your call (an empty list if none), and a rationale of one or two sentences. Then give a short impression. Do not explain what the findings are. Cite cases by their ID exactly as written, e.g. CXR316. Give the probability with two decimals as your honest estimate; for subtle, borderline or partly obscured appearances, use intermediate values rather than a fixed low value. Clinical indication: Chronic airway obstruction. Similar cases (most similar first): Case CXR929 (similarity 0.958): FINDINGS: No change lung XXXX. XXXX opacities are present in the right lower lobe. No focal infiltrates. Heart and mediastinum are unremarkable. Aorta normal. IMPRESSION: Findings of COPD with right lung base focal atelectasis. No evidence for failure or pneumonia. Case CXR822 (similarity 0.958): FINDINGS: The lungs remain hyperexpanded. There are persistent XXXX bilateral lower lobe opacities, XXXX subsegmental atelectasis and scarring. No XXXX focal infiltrate is identified. There is no pleural effusion or pneumothorax. Normal heart size. There are minimal degenerative changes of the spine. IMPRESSION: 1. No acute findings. 2. Bibasilar subsegmental atelectasis or scarring. 3. Emphysema. Case CXR2192 (similarity 0.956): FINDINGS: No focal lung consolidation. No pneumothorax or pleural effusion.Heart size and pulmonary vascularity are within normal limits.Minimal degenerative changes of the thoracic spine. The previously
described XXXX deformity in the midthoracic spine is again seen. There is subcutaneous shunt catheter tubing along the anterior chest wall IMPRESSION: No acute cardiopulmonary process. Case CXR2861 (similarity 0.954): FINDINGS: The heart size and pulmonary vascularity appear within normal limits. The lungs are free of focal airspace disease. No pleural effusion or pneumothorax is seen. IMPRESSION: 1. No evidence of active disease. Case CXR2633 (similarity 0.953): FINDINGS: Heart size is normal. Prior calcified granulomatous disease. On the lateral view in the anterior costophrenic XXXX, there is a 2.1 x 2 cm nodular density which seems to be present previously but is more nodular in appearance on this examination. No pleural effusion or pneumothorax. Endplate degenerative changes of the thoracolumbar spine and mild scoliosis are unchanged. IMPRESSION: 2.1 cm nodular density in the anterior costophrenic XXXX on the lateral view, which could represent overlapping shadows or actual pulmonary nodule. Recommend followup with chest CT. Case CXR2379 (similarity 0.952): FINDINGS: Cardiomediastinal silhouette is within normal limits of size and appearance. Lungs are hyperlucent and hyperexpanded. Negative for focal airspace disease or consolidation. Negative for pneumothorax or pleural effusion. Limited evaluation reveals no acute abnormality. IMPRESSION: Stable chronic lung changes without acute cardiopulmonary abnormality. Case CXR1378 (similarity 0.952): FINDINGS: Heart size is normal. Cardiomediastinal silhouette is normal in contour. The lungs are clear bilaterally without pleural effusion or pneumothorax. No pulmonary nodules. Bony structures are intact. IMPRESSION: Negative for acute abnormality. Case CXR2253 (similarity 0.951): FINDINGS: There is hyperinflation of the lungs but they are clear. The heart and mediastinum are normal. The skeletal structures are normal. There are bilateral breast prostheses. IMPRESSION: COPD. Case CXR2364 (similarity 0.950): FINDINGS: The lungs are clear. There is hyperexpansion of the lungs suggesting underlying emphysema. The heart and pulmonary XXXX appear normal. Pleural spaces are clear. Mediastinal contours are normal. IMPRESSION: No acute cardiopulmonary disease Case CXR2445 (similarity 0.950): FINDINGS: The heart is normal in size. The mediastinum is unremarkable. The lungs are clear. IMPRESSION: No acute disease. The patient's frontal chest X-ray follows.
